summary.intent: Plan, execute, and ship Phase 62 ('Unified Node Codec Core Keystone') of CipherBox — replacing legacy FolderMetadata/FileMetadata with a unified Node discriminated union with dual-sealed bodies, generation-based AAD, vault blob v3 hard-cut, frozen golden vectors, and downstream compile-gate migrations across the pnpm monorepo.
summary.outcome: Phase 62 fully planned (9 plans/7 waves, plan-checker PASSED 6/6), executed sequentially (190 core tests green, all consumers brought to compile-only per D-01), and shipped as PR #578 — with a CI typecheck regression in .mts E2E helper scripts discovered and fixed mid-ship, plus two in-scope hardening fixes applied during CodeRabbit/Greptile triage.

repo: tests/sdk-e2e CI job runs on any src-change PR (gated by changes.outputs.src == 'true') but was not quarantined by the execute-phase subagents — a systematic blind spot: executors quarantine unit suites but miss the integration suite at tests/sdk-e2e/

tsconfig.scripts.json typechecks .mts desktop E2E helper scripts (established in #532/#537) — these are NOT covered by pnpm typecheck's package-scoped typecheck and fail only in CI's dedicated Typecheck job
CodeRabbit CLI with --agent produces suggestions that are frequently already-implemented no-ops; always diff suggestions against current code before applying
CodeRabbit posts findings in review body (not inline threads) when the diff exceeds ~136 files — reviewThreads GraphQL query returns 0; Greptile posts actual inline threads on this repo
After gh pr create, github-actions[bot] pushes a chore(release) commit — must git fetch + rebase before any subsequent push or it's rejected
GSD commit helper query commit returns commit_failed while the commit actually landed — always verify with git log --oneline -1, never retry blindly
gh pr edit fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — patch PR body via gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file
landing/.astro/ is gitignored/untracked (0 tracked files on origin/main) — local eslint failures there are invisible to CI's fresh checkout and can be safely ignored

code.finding: unsealNode lacked a fail-closed guard on envelope schema/aeadVersion — these plaintext fields are not AAD-bound, so a v1 reader previously accepted unknown future envelope versions silently. Fixed by rejecting unsupported schema/aeadVersion values before decryption.

deserializeVaultBlobV3 used subarray() for readKey/writeKey extraction, which aliases the caller's input buffer. Changed to slice() so the deserialized struct owns its buffers — safer under the D-09 zeroization requirement.

FilePointer-era E2E helper scripts (edit-filepointer.mts, rename-folder.mts, verify-filepointer.mts, bump-ipns-sequence.ts) reference retired types and cannot be migrated until read-chain un-stubs (phases 63-65). Added explicit exclude entries to prevent CI Typecheck failure.
base64 encode/decode helpers are duplicated across node/seal.ts, node/encode.ts, and node/decode.ts — acceptable under freeze-first discipline (D-04) but should be consolidated post-keystone.

workflow: Sequential executor on the main tree is strongly preferred over worktree isolation for pnpm monorepos — the cross-package dist chain (core→sdk-core→sdk→web) is far simpler without per-worktree pnpm install overhead
The D-02 gate must explicitly run scripts typecheck via the correct local tsc path — using bash -lc 'tsc ...' silently exits 127 (PATH miss) and masks real failures, leading to CI regressions

When a local typecheck step reports a known flake (TS2688 @types/node), always verify whether there are *other* errors beyond the flake before dismissing it — run pnpm install first to relink @types/node
Git commit signing: if the hook hangs past the timeout budget, the commit may still land (the signer wedges after write); check git log before concluding failure or retrying
For CodeRabbit CLI --agent suggestions: grep the suggestion's distinguishing string against current source before applying — many suggestions target code the executors already wrote defensively

todo files under .planning/todos/pending/ are the correct capture point for out-of-scope/risky findings from security auditors, validators, and code reviewers — consistently reference file path + destination phase

GSD plan-checker revision loop (max 3 iterations): the checker reliably finds structural issues (split oversized plans, move vectors to committed files, add exit-code guards) on the first pass; one revision round is typically sufficient

friction: Local @types/node not linked in node_modules — masked the real .mts scripts typecheck regression as 'the known TS2688 flake'; this caused a CI failure on PR #578 that required a mid-ship hotfix
bash -lc 'tsc ...' invocation bug (PATH miss → exit 127) caused the D-02 gate's scripts typecheck step to silently not run, masking the .mts regression entirely during local validation
GSD commit helper consistently reports commit_failed for commits that actually land — requires git log verification after every commit, adding friction to the autonomous loop
Git signing hangs silently post-commit-write (1Password signer wedges) — commits land unsigned without a clear failure signal; only discoverable via git log --format='%G?'
CodeRabbit CLI --agent produces 59 findings for a 136-file diff, the majority of which are already-implemented no-ops — high triage cost for low yield
CodeRabbit PR-level review fails to post inline threads when diff > ~136 files — no authoritative thread list to resolve; fell back to Greptile threads
Release bot chore(release) commit requires a git fetch + rebase before every push after PR creation — easy to forget in an autonomous loop
